technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Data GemFire as the primary integration layer for GemFire interactions.
Implement the GemFire message-channel binder using Spring Cloud Stream's binder SPI.
Leverage Spring Cloud Data Flow's existing module registry and stream repository abstractions for GemFire integration.
Design tap functionality using GemFire's eventing capabilities to fork data streams without impacting the primary pipeline.
Use Spring Boot auto-configuration for GemFire components to simplify deployment and configuration.
assumptions: The development team has prior experience with Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data Flow, and GemFire.
GemFire server instances and dependencies are pre-configured and accessible.
Documentation tasks (U5, U6) can be developed in parallel with code implementation.
The DSL/Shell for tap support (U8) will reuse existing Spring Cloud Data Flow shell infrastructure.
All user stories are independent and can be implemented in any order.

activities.activity_description: Define the integration points for GemFire in the binder, SPI, repository, and module registry. Plan tap functionality and documentation structure.
Implement the GemFire binder for Spring Cloud Stream, including message conversion and GemFire pub-sub/queue integration.
Develop GemFire-based SPI for orchestrating data microservices, including data serialization and GemFire-specific configurations.
Implement a stream repository backed by GemFire for storing and managing data pipelines.
Set up GemFire as a module registry, enabling CRUD operations for stream modules.
